data.body_html:
Imagine a calm Marbella morning: the sun glints off the Mediterranean, a light breeze carries the scent of the sea, and you're sipping cava on a luxury motor yacht. Ahead, a pod of wild dolphins arcs through the waves. This is the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2035 — a two-hour escape from Puerto Banús that combines wildlife spotting with a relaxed brunch on the water. Priced at €1,299 for the full charter (up to 12 guests), it's an intimate, all-inclusive experience with a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and Spanish IVA covered. No hidden costs, no crowds — just you, your group, and the dolphins.

Why choose a dolphin watching brunch cruise in Marbella?

The Costa del Sol is one of Europe's best spots for dolphin watching. Resident pods of common and bottlenose dolphins hunt in the nutrient-rich waters off Marbella, often within a few nautical miles of Puerto Banús. A morning cruise offers the calmest seas and highest sighting probability — our skippers report sightings on over 90% of trips. Unlike larger dolphin-watching boats, our private yacht charter means you enjoy the experience in comfort and privacy, with a dedicated crew focused on your group.

What's included in the 2035 brunch cruise

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and a light brunch with drinks. The brunch features fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, premium coffee, juices, and cava or white wine. Soft drinks, beer, and water are available throughout. All prices include Spanish IVA (21%) — no surprises. You just need to bring sun protection and your camera.

Yacht options for your dolphin watching cruise

We typically use the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) for this experience. Its spacious flybridge offers panoramic views ideal for spotting dolphins, while the saloon and aft deck provide shade and comfort. Depending on availability, other yachts from our fleet — such as the Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) or Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax) — may be used. All are modern, well-maintained, and equipped for a safe, enjoyable cruise.

Itinerary: a typical morning on the water

The cruise departs from Puerto Banús at 10:00. After a safety briefing, you'll head west towards the Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés areas, where dolphins frequently hunt. The skipper will navigate to known hotspots while keeping a respectful distance. Brunch is served as you cruise. After about 90 minutes, you'll return to port, arriving around 12:00. The exact route depends on dolphin activity and weather conditions.

Best time of year for dolphin watching in Marbella

Dolphins are present year-round off Marbella, but the best visibility and sea conditions occur from April to October. Summer months (June to September) offer the calmest seas and warmest temperatures (25-30°C). Spring and autumn are also excellent, with fewer crowds and still-mild weather. Winter cruises are possible but sea conditions can be choppier; sightings remain common.

How to book your Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2035

Booking is simple via WhatsApp. Send us your preferred date, number of guests, and any dietary requirements. We'll confirm availability, suggest the best yacht, and send payment details. A 50% deposit secures your booking. We recommend booking at least a week in advance, especially in high season. For more information on all our experiences, visit our Boat Rental Marbella hub.
